modules.title: 1. Textiles with a purpose
modules.timing: Week 1; approximately 180 minutes, timetable Teacher to confirm

sections.title: 1.1 Textiles are everywhere
content_descriptors: Identify characteristics and properties of materials; outline factors affecting product design; investigate products developed by designers and producers.
sections.learning_intention: Explain how textile products respond to users and purposes, then frame a respectful cause-based design direction.
sections.learning_sequence: Introduce textiles as systems of fibres, yarns, fabrics and components. Analyse the bucket hat as an apparel product, identify user needs and discuss how colour, imagery and material choices can communicate a respectful cause.
sections.working_scientifically: Not applicable to Technology 7–8; design and production process: Identifying and defining; researching users, purpose and context.
sections.evidence: Activity 1 purpose gallery; three written responses; 30 section checks; initial folio evidence.
sections.formative_checks: 10 adjacent section questions plus one guided written response
sections.adjustments: Use real textile examples, labelled visuals, word banks, oral rehearsal and a reduced set of cause prompts where appropriate.
sections.resources: Module 1 webpage and PowerPoint, purpose gallery image, videos, Activity 1 and folio.

modules.title: 2. Safe textile work
modules.timing: Week 2; approximately 180 minutes, timetable Teacher to confirm

sections.title: 2.1 Practical-room routines
content_descriptors: Use tools, materials, techniques, technologies and processes to develop practical skills; demonstrate safe practices when selecting and using materials, technologies and processes.
sections.learning_intention: Select specific controls for textile-room hazards and demonstrate readiness for teacher-supervised practical work.
sections.learning_sequence: Explicitly teach entry routines, workstation organisation, sharp and hot tool controls and sewing-machine stop-work triggers. Students analyse hazards, justify tool selection and rehearse the teacher-approved readiness routine.
sections.working_scientifically: Not applicable to Technology 7–8; design and production process: Researching risks; selecting controls; planning a safe workflow.
sections.evidence: Activity 2 safety and tools audit; readiness explanations; three written responses; 30 section checks.
sections.formative_checks: 10 adjacent section questions plus one guided written response
sections.adjustments: Provide labelled tool images, visual safety sequences, repeated demonstration and individual checking before equipment use.
sections.resources: Module 2 webpage and PowerPoint, safe-workstation image, machine-parts visual, videos and Activity 2.

modules.title: 3. Visual messages
modules.timing: Week 3; approximately 180 minutes, timetable Teacher to confirm

sections.title: 3.1 Colour communicates
content_descriptors: Use sketching and drawing techniques to communicate ideas and solutions; communicate development using annotations; outline factors affecting product design.
sections.learning_intention: Use colour, imagery and technique deliberately to communicate a clear, respectful message on fabric.
sections.learning_sequence: Analyse colour meanings as context-dependent, investigate symbol clarity and ownership, and compare decorative techniques as communication choices. Students develop an original palette, symbol and technique proposal.

sections.formative_checks: 10 adjacent section questions plus one guided written response
sections.adjustments: Offer high-contrast examples, symbol simplification templates, curated references and alternatives to fine-motor drawing.
sections.resources: Module 3 webpage and PowerPoint, colour and symbol visuals, videos and Activity 3.

modules.title: 4. Define the challenge

content_descriptors: Outline factors affecting the design of products and solutions; apply critical and creative thinking to assess ideas and quality solutions; document design processes.
sections.learning_intention: Convert the project situation into a user-focused brief with observable criteria and realistic constraints.
sections.learning_sequence: Model the difference between situation, brief, criteria and constraints. Students identify the intended user and cause, rewrite the brief in their own words and establish measurable or observable success criteria.
sections.working_scientifically: Not applicable to Technology 7–8; design and production process: Identifying and defining; establishing criteria for success; recording constraints.
sections.evidence: Activity 4 brief builder; criteria and constraints; three written responses; section checks.
sections.formative_checks: 10 adjacent section questions plus one guided written response
sections.adjustments: Use worked and non-worked examples, sentence starters, oral rehearsal and criteria sorting cards.

modules.title: 6. Fibres, fabrics and sustainability

sections.learning_sequence: Teach fibre-yarn-fabric relationships and compare woven structures, cotton, polyester and blends. Students connect performance and care properties to the approved hat materials and evaluate practical waste and durability actions.

sections.evidence: Activity 6 material decision report; cotton/polyester comparison; sustainability actions; section checks.
sections.formative_checks: 10 adjacent section questions plus one guided written response
sections.adjustments: Use tactile samples, property cards, comparison frames, accessible texts and teacher-curated source extracts.
sections.resources: Module 6 webpage and PowerPoint, fibre comparison visual, videos and Activity 6.

modules.title: 7. Decorative technique trials

content_descriptors: Create prototypes, models and samples to test materials and production processes; justify selection and use of tools, materials, techniques and technologies.
sections.learning_intention: Conduct controlled decorative trials and justify the technique selected for the final fabric.
sections.learning_sequence: Model a fair sample test and evidence log. Students trial teacher-approved decorative techniques on comparable fabric, record observations, identify a success criterion and select or refine a method for the final hat.

sections.adjustments: Offer pre-cut sample pieces, larger-scale trials, visual step cards, alternative recording modes and additional supervised practice.

sections.working_scientifically: Not applicable to Technology 7–8; design and production process: Testing; evaluating; reflecting; communicating improvements.
sections.evidence: Activity 10 evaluation and designer statement; completed folio; final product and process evidence; section checks.
sections.formative_checks: 10 adjacent section questions plus one guided written response
sections.adjustments: Use criterion-evidence-judgement-improvement frames, oral planning, speech-to-text, labelled photographs and chunked evaluation categories.
sections.resources: Module 10 webpage and PowerPoint, evaluation and designer-statement visuals, videos, Activity 10 and folio.
